acceptanceCovered: SC-001 an unauthenticated visitor to a protected route is redirected to /login — proven by e2e/auth-guard.spec.ts across /, /about, /countdown, /sun-kudos, /award-info; RED before proxy.ts existed, GREEN after.
SC-003 the Google button is disabled and exposes aria-busy while authenticating — proven by e2e/login-click-contract.spec.ts asserting both states while the authorize navigation is held pending.

SC-005 a failed or cancelled sign-in renders a localized error in a role=alert region — proven by e2e/login-error-state.spec.ts; copy comes from the login i18n namespace in en and vi, no hard-coded string.

SC-006 the button click issues an authorize request with provider=google and a query-string-free redirect_to — proven by e2e/login-click-contract.spec.ts with exact equality on redirect_to = http://127.0.0.1:3000/auth/callback.

SC-007 the callback never reflects an inbound next or redirect_to into a redirect target — proven by live curl probes: next and redirect_to set to https://evil.test produced 307 to /login?error=oauth_failed with zero occurrences of evil.test in any response header.
regressionChecked: Baseline repair did not alter runtime behaviour: react-i18next v17's only breaking change is <Trans> auto-key serialization and this codebase uses zero <Trans> — verified by grep; only useTranslation, I18nextProvider and initReactI18next are imported.
Removing the dead next-intl plugin from next.config.ts kept images.remotePatterns verbatim; pnpm build succeeds and all 7 routes still compile.
NEXT_LOCALE survives the proxy response rebuild — the guard returns the rebuilt supabaseResponse which carries forward request cookies; app renders lang=vi as before.
Adding e2e/**/*.ts to a tsconfig include that already globbed **/*.ts did not break pnpm typecheck (exit 0).
Prettier reformatting was confined to files this change touched; ~140 pre-existing unformatted files were deliberately left untouched to avoid diff churn.
supabase/config.toml edit was a single allow-list line; no migration, no db reset, no container restart — the pre-existing 11-container stack and its 9 migrations were left intact.
unproven: SC-002 an authenticated visitor to /login is redirected away to the post-login target — the FR-102 branch exists in lib/supabase/proxy.ts but has never been exercised against a real session. Unautomatable under the agreed Docker-free E2E scope because the guard calls getUser(), which round-trips to GoTrue.
SC-004 a successful sign-in lands the user on /countdown before launch or /about after — the happy path has never been executed; it needs real Google OAuth credentials.
FR-401 the selected language survives the whole sign-in redirect chain — only the proxy hop was reasoned about; the full 3-hop chain through Google has never been walked.

findings.summary: Both guard redirect branches returned a bare NextResponse.redirect, discarding cookies Supabase had refreshed during the request. With enable_refresh_token_rotation=true this strands the browser on a rotated-away refresh token and causes random sign-outs. Fixed by routing both branches through redirectPreservingCookies. Found by code reading; no test could catch it because a Docker-free suite never triggers a rotation.

The callback built absolute redirect URLs, which Next resolves to its own configured hostname under next start regardless of the inbound Host header. A user signing in at 127.0.0.1:3000 had the session cookie written for 127.0.0.1 then was redirected to localhost:3000, a different cookie host, so sign-in silently never stuck. A first fix using request.nextUrl.clone() was verified NOT to work; fixed by switching every exit to redirect() from next/navigation, which emits a host-relative Location.

handleLogin had no try/catch. createClient() throws on missing env vars and signInWithOAuth can reject outright, leaving loading true so the button stayed disabled behind a spinner with no message and no retry. Fixed by wrapping the body; success deliberately does not reset loading because the browser is navigating away.

exchangeCodeForSession was unguarded and Route Handlers are not covered by error.tsx boundaries, so a thrown exception produced a bare 500 instead of the promised /login?error=oauth_failed redirect. Fixed by extracting exchangeCode() so the try/catch cannot enclose a redirect() call, which signals by throwing NEXT_REDIRECT and would otherwise be swallowed.

The document claimed protected pages perform a defense-in-depth getUser() check; grep confirmed none of the four protected pages do. Reframed as a known gap and recommended hardening rather than deleted, because the Next.js 16 Proxy docs warn Proxy alone is not an authorization boundary.

The / route case is a tautology: app/page.tsx is an unconditional redirect('/login') stub, so that assertion passes with or without the guard and can never catch a regression on /. The other four routes provide genuine coverage.

next-intl remains a declared dependency with zero importers after its build wiring was removed in the baseline repair. Harmless but dead weight; removal deferred to avoid widening this change's scope.
